metadata.description: Standalone Claude Code marketplace hosting the ai-ready plugin — audit codebases for AI-readiness, apply ROI-prioritized improvements, and run an autonomous maker→checker→deterministic-rubric verification loop, all in one plugin. Supports both multi-module and single-module (package-as-module) layouts. v0.2.0+: config-driven frontmatter-aware INDEX + lazy-load user/auto split. v0.3.0+: config rubric section makes scoring respect project reality (docs/design as ADR, springdoc as API contract, .claude hooks as verification gate). v0.4.0+: apply guards human-adopted docs (generators refuse to overwrite files lacking the auto-gen signature; per-doc diff-confirm loop). v0.4.2+: INDEX generation respects .gitignore — only tracked or unignored .md is indexed, so generated artifacts and .claude/commands no longer pollute INDEX; non-git dirs fall back to a full walk. v0.5.0+: apply maintains docs surgically — the doc-touching scripts gather facts only (--json, read-only) and the AI adds/updates just what changed while preserving human curation, instead of wholesale overwriting. v0.6.0+: the former loop-engine plugin is folded into ai-ready — /loop-run, /loop-review, /loop-lessons + loop-checker/loop-lesson-synthesizer agents + the _loop-engine scoring shell ship in the same plugin, so one install covers the whole audit→apply→verify cycle and the loop reads/appends the docs/ANTIPATTERNS.md that ai-ready writes. v0.8.0+: the loop-build skill adds multi-phase autonomous build-out — it wraps loop-run's checker+rubric verdict engine in an outer phase loop where the maker is a per-phase subagent (continued via SendMessage within a phase) so many phases build out unattended while the orchestrator stays coding-free. v0.8.1+: loop-build fail-loud-validates phases.json before the unattended traversal — a jq assertion rejects a malformed decomposition (empty/non-array .phases, missing name/steps/ac_cmd, or an out-of-enum status) with exit 65 so a corrupt spec halts for a human instead of silently mis-traversing. v0.8.2+: the loop skills and loop-checker recover findings via a deterministic orchestrator-named output file rather than scraping the checker's final chat message, since a background/unattended session never delivers a subagent's final text inline; loop-checker's no-write Bash rule gains one narrow carve-out (that single findings path only), the orchestrator clears the file before each spin, and a fail-loud guard rejects an empty/missing findings file instead of silently passing. v0.8.3+: wiring & context-hygiene batch — the freshness Stop hook is self-contained (the copied .sh locates freshness_check.py next to itself and audit copies the .py too, so a project-context hook no longer dies on unset CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT); convention-docs/knowledge-layer/LOCAL-rubric paths are passed to the checker and lesson-synthesizer IN THE PROMPT (env vars never reach subagents, so the old wiring silently degraded every checker to the no-convention-docs path); loop-run persists brake values and detected commands to a params.env re-derived at the top of every step (a fresh shell per Bash call was silently disarming the iteration/time brake) and counts gate-failure re-entries against the brake; loop-build scopes stall state and the gate counter per phase and enforces the per-phase history split by re-pointing params.env (a prior phase's floor no longer manufactures false STALLED verdicts); the re-derivation pointer is per-branch (.active-{branch}) so an interleaved second loop cannot hijack a paused loop's state, params.env is sourced with set -a so LOCAL-rubric env reaches the scoring child processes, and the gate-failure counter increments self-contained from its file and codifies orchestrator context hygiene (never read findings/evidence prose inline — score summaries only, hand the maker the scored-file path instead of pasting findings, update phases.json via jq not Read/Edit, and prefer starting loop-build in a fresh session after design); decide/stall fail-loud-validate their input contracts; npm's default test stub is not adopted as a gate; loop-review detects the base branch before diffing and isolates its findings file per branch; the BASE rubric's security narrowing to IDOR-only is re-labeled as a c8c-api LOCAL decision (BASE stays broad). v0.8.4+: loop-checker and loop-lesson-synthesizer no longer pin model: opus in frontmatter — they inherit the calling session's model by default, overridable per invocation via the Agent tool's model param. v0.8.5+: loop-build's maker becomes a dedicated loop-maker agent whose frontmatter sets model: opus as a default tier below the session model (production work intentionally downgraded while the checker inherits the session model as the quality gate); the Agent call's model param still overrides per phase. v0.8.6+: loop-build's PASS branch makes maker termination explicit — the orchestrator sends a final 'phase done — terminate' SendMessage and never re-enters that maker, and loop-maker ends its turn on that notice; passed-phase makers no longer linger as waiting teammates. v0.8.7+: inject_lazy_load_index drops auto-table rows whose document is already linked from the user section — the root CLAUDE.md is always-loaded, so a doc listed in both the hand-written and the generated table costs its duplicate every session (12 rows / ~1,558 chars in one repo). Link targets are compared with trailing slashes normalized, only a row whose every target is already covered is dropped, and when all detected docs are covered the auto block renders a one-line note instead of an empty table — automating what previously needed hand-maintained config.override_hardcoded entries. v0.8.8+: the root `## 모듈 맵` stub listing length is config-driven — `module_map.root_stub_limit` (default 10, unchanged); 0 keeps only the catalog link and drops the per-module excerpt. The root doc is always-loaded and each module's one-line summary already lives in its own CLAUDE.md (auto-loaded when that module is opened), so the excerpt is duplicate context in repos that link enough paths elsewhere (~1,800 chars in one repo). Because audit's "root doc references 3+ module/doc paths" rule counts that listing as a reference source in some repos, the default is unchanged and setting 0 prints a notice instead of silently losing points. Bad values (negative, bool, non-int) fall back to the default rather than breaking generation. v0.8.9+: the root-size rule and the trigger table are re-aimed at always-loaded cost. The root-size rule measures the root CLAUDE.md in **bytes** (<=8,000 full, <=12,000 partial) instead of lines — a Korean markdown root packs a whole table row or paragraph into one line, so a real 46-line root doc weighing 12,029 bytes (one bullet alone 2,002 chars) took full marks under the old <=200-line rule while it kept growing; bytes weight Hangul 3:1 against ASCII, closer to token share. The evidence string carries both bytes and lines (kept even on a 0-point verdict) so audit history shows the trend. Repos that passed the line rule may now score lower — that break in the trend line is the intended correction, not a regression. inject_lazy_load_index folds "the filename IS the trigger" documents (COMMANDS/NAMING/TESTING/ARCHITECTURE/ANTIPATTERNS/INDEX) out of the auto table into one link line: 0.8.7 removed only *duplicate* rows, leaving rows that were not duplicates yet told the reader nothing a directory listing does not. The links stay on that line, so the path-reference rule's count is unaffected — and that rule saturates at 3 references anyway, so a long table earns no points while costing context every session. --json facts gain `self_evident` so the AI maintenance path splits rows the same way the writer does. v0.9.0+: the minimum-content gate is raised and widened so a repo of stubs can no longer score full marks. An adversarial audit found a repo of twenty-one three-line stub files scoring 100/100 "Agentic-ready": the gate was a loose 3 non-blank lines, and several rules bypassed it entirely, checking only file existence or a regex match. The gate now requires **400 bytes AND 8 non-blank lines together** — either condition alone is trivially gamed (one very long line, or many one-character lines) — and it newly covers per-module CLAUDE.md coverage, the index/MOC file, ADR directories, API-contract files, outcome-metric artifacts, and the two category-2 keyword rules. The DO-NOT rule is staircased by guide-line count (3+ lines full, 1-2 partial). Two upper-bound-only rules gain floors: a root doc under 800 bytes and module docs averaging under 10 lines now score partial, where before a 0-byte root and three-line module docs took full marks. Every rule reference in the scripts and RUBRIC.md is now by exact rule name instead of number — the rubric table has no number column, so the numbers had no defining coordinate system and `Rule 1.5` was already dead. Measured: the stub repo drops from 100 to 52 while two real repos stay at 53 and 71, which is the intended asymmetry; treat the v0.9.0 boundary as another deliberate break in the trend line. v0.9.1+: a second adversarial review closes the bypasses v0.9.0 missed. Root-doc path references must point at existing non-stub targets (three links to nonexistent files scored 4/4); binary files fail the minimum-content gate (NUL sniff in the first 8 KB) and the directory gate counts only text-doc extensions, so a stray image next to stub ADRs no longer clears it; the update-protocol keyword must live in a non-stub doc; settings hooks whose commands point at missing repo-relative scripts score partial (a dead config is not a gate — PATH commands stay unchecked); config build_deps declarations must be >=4 chars and sit on a dependency-declaration line (declaring `plugins` against an empty gradle manifest converted 2->5); antipatterns doc_hints upgrade past a stub-file partial the same way naming hints do; and the report discloses config-earned points so self-reported credit is visible at a glance. Measured: the stub repo drops 52 -> 38 (AI-blind), the config+junk attack ceiling drops 63 -> 46 without crossing a grade band, and the two real repos stay at 53 and 71. v0.9.2+: doc-alignment batch from the same review. The generated .ai-ready/README.md writes its artifact table from what actually exists in the output directory — audit does not produce dashboard.html or scaffolds/ (dashboard.py and apply do), yet the old README listed them unconditionally and claimed they refresh on every run, so a reader who re-ran only audit trusted a stale dashboard; absent artifacts now get generation instructions instead of table rows, and the overwrite note says dashboard.html refreshes only via dashboard.py. apply's root-doc drafting instruction is re-denominated in bytes (800-8,000, matching the root-size rule) — it still said '50-150 lines' while scoring moved to bytes in v0.8.9, and the v0.8.9 evidence case itself (46 lines = 12,029 bytes) shows lines can pass while bytes fail. MOC is defined at first use in RUBRIC.md (Map of Content), a malformed bold marker in the apply mapping table is fixed, and the v0.9.1 scoring note is corrected to claim settings-hook command targets only (CI configs are exempt — their working directory is unknowable). v0.9.3+: DO-NOT full marks require repo-specific pointers. The staircase counts a guidance line toward full marks only if it also carries a backtick code reference, a path, or a CamelCase/snake_case identifier — counting bare keyword lines made writing '금지' three times the optimal strategy (measured: it scored 5/5). Keyword farming now caps at the 3/5 partial, and vague-but-real rules keep partial instead of being zeroed. Measured before shipping: agent kept 50/92 counted lines, c8c-api 242/378 — both far above the 3-line bar, so real scores did not move. v0.9.4+: a failed gate becomes a work queue instead of console noise. When the build, test, or lint gate fails, loop-run redirects its output to a file and _loop-engine/gate_parse.py turns it into one JSON item per line (kind, file, line_number, message, raw), which the maker works through in the order compile-error, test-failure, lint-violation. Previously the whole build log landed in the orchestrator's context every cycle and was re-read on the next one. A non-empty gate queue now takes precedence over the findings file, because a failed gate means the checker never ran that cycle and the findings file still holds the previous cycle's values. The parser never emits an empty queue: with no recognised format it keeps the output tail as one gate-output-unparsed item, since an empty queue reads as a pass. Formats came from real output rather than memory — Kotlin 2.x puts no colon after the column number, so a remembered regex would have matched nothing. v0.9.5+: loop-run's maker is a fresh subagent every cycle rather than the orchestrator session itself, matching what the other three loop skills already did — the session spins subagents, runs the scoring shell, reads the verdict, and branches, and writes no code of its own. The task definition must be a file, and maker and checker are pointed at the same one so the two never work from divergent summaries; when the agreement lives only in chat the orchestrator writes one brief and has a human confirm it before the first cycle, the single human gate in an otherwise unattended run. What crosses cycles is the working tree plus per-finding repeat markers derived from history.jsonl, not a conversation. Before each gate the loop verifies the tree actually changed, because a maker's report can be wrong where the tree cannot — an unchanged tree is a stall signal, not a cycle. A maker that ends in blocked goes to AWAIT_USER instead of to another maker. loop-maker is now shared by loop-run and loop-build, with the maker's lifetime — cycle versus phase — the only difference left between them.
